gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's own instruction from its MagSafe Charger support page: if a case holds cards, remove them before charging or make sure they aren't between the back of the iPhone and the charger. That condition is the one compatibility rule that splits the candidates. A front-flap folio (the Nomad Modern Leather Folio, which Nomad lists for iPhone 17 as 'MagSafe & Qi2 charging compatible') keeps the cards on the screen side by design. A rear-slot card case (Smartish Wallet Slayer) can't meet it, and Smartish says that line is 'not compatible with MagSafe or wireless chargers'.
standout_why: I compared against Macworld (cited, updated 2026-09-10) and Apple's Accessory Design Guidelines PDF (cited). Macworld lists no card or wallet case in the part of the page I could read, so it has no card-plus-charging pairing for iPhone 17. ChatGPT already gave the shopper the general rule by citing the PDF ('advise against rear credit-card pockets'), and its first answer described the Nomad cards as sitting in the front flap. So the idea is partly there already. What the rivals lack: Apple's consumer-facing wording that cards may stay in the case as long as they are not between the phone and the charger, which makes the front-flap folio the compliant design rather than an 'unverified' one; and the maker's 'not compatible with MagSafe or wireless chargers' exclusion for the Wallet Slayer line. The PDF is a design guide written for accessory makers, not a shopper instruction.
decides: It supports the Nomad Modern Leather Folio as the pick for 'card holder plus MagSafe charging without taking anything off'. On the charger the cards sit in the flap over the screen, not between the phone's back and the charger, which is Apple's stated condition. It also confirms the 'No (cable only)' cells for both Wallet Slayers. Caveat: Nomad does not say in writing that charging works with the flap closed and cards inside, so the page should present this as Apple's rule applied to the folio design, not as a Nomad claim or a test result. Nomad is $74 today, down from $99.
candidates: Smartish Gripmunk with MagSafe + MagSafe wallet

findings.label: Apple rule for cards in a case on a MagSafe Charger
findings.value: "If you have a case that holds any of these sensitive items, remove them before charging or make sure that they aren't between the back of your device and the charger." Also: "Don't place credit cards, security badges, passports, or key fobs between your iPhone and MagSafe Charger" because it "might damage magnetic strips or RFID chips".
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Quoted verbatim from the page. The page says nothing on case thickness, metal cases or Apple's own wallets.
